messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (gateway) — spike started ~2026-03-14T11:58Z. Current 5xx: 18%, p95 latency: 2.1s, queue depth: 78. Paging @jamie.oncall and @sarah-sre :rotating_light:

jamie.oncall: ack, I'm on it. any recent deploys or config changes?

deploy-bot: rollout complete: r-2026-03-14-1158 -> model-routing-config v2 (max_sequence=2048) applied to region=us-west-2.

miguel-runtime: that rollout bumped default max_seq for hosted models — likely larger token windows -> bigger batches and KV growth. seeing batcher pool saturation in telemetry.

jamie.oncall: logs snippet from gateway / batcher:```
[2026-03-14T12:03:21Z] gateway ERROR upstream=502 batcher=pool-42 queue_len=78 hol=true caller=batcher/scheduler.go:214
[2026-03-14T12:03:22Z] batcher WARN enqueue_delay=320ms batch_size=64 kv_cache_bytes=5.1GB pool=pool-42
```

carla-product: CS: we have 3 enterprise customers reporting intermittent 502s in the last 10m, some pages already. They're seeing request failures for long prompts.

jamie.oncall: hypothesis: head-of-line (HOL) blocking in pool-42 due to a few long sequences creating oversized batches, increasing per-token processing and KV growth -> queue-backed timeouts + 5xx. Need quick mitigations: 1) protect gateway (short-term throttles / circuit), 2) reduce batch impact (route long seqs to fallback model or smaller shard), 3) scale pool / evict kv caches.

miguel-runtime: agreed. I'm pushing emergency config: reduce batch max tokens and enable fallback routing to smaller model for requests with seq > 1024. commands:```
# reduce batcher token cap (applies in 60s)
redwoodctl config set batcher.pool-42.BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=1024 --env=prod
# enable fallback route for large-seq requests
redwoodctl route update gateway --fallback-model=redwood/opt-1.4-small-quant --seq-threshold=1024
```

jamie.oncall: running now. also scaling pool replicas while we flatten queue:```
kubectl scale deploy/batcher-pool-42 --replicas=8 -n redwood-inference
```

miguel-runtime: also evicting hot KV ranges to free memory (this will drop some cached prefixes, safe):```
curl -X POST "http://batcher-admin.pool-42.svc.cluster.local/cache/evict?percent=30" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

jamie.oncall: executed config change and scale. queue_len dropped from 78 -> 30 in 45s. 5xx dropped to 9% and p95 to 1.3s. fallback route successfully created.

carla-product: telling CS: we see error rates improving, routing change applied. CS will keep customers updated. estimated impacted calls: ~4% of production traffic at peak, mostly long-prompt workloads.

sarah-sre: good progress. recommend enabling temporary gateway-level rate limit for multi-k requesters to blunt new long-run inputs while we stabilize. to enable:```
redwoodctl rate-limit set gateway --route=/v1/generate --max-requests-per-min=1200 --scope=org --priority=emergency
```

jamie.oncall: enabled the gateway limit. also toggled an emergency circuit to fail fast for requests with sequence > 4096 to protect downstream.

deploy-bot: note: there is an in-progress canary rollback candidate r-2026-03-14-1145 if a config rollback is requested.

miguel-runtime: long-term fixes: 1) change scheduler to prefer small-batch packing for bursty long sequences, 2) KV cache soft-eviction for stale prefixes, 3) more aggressive per-customer throttles. For now, fallback routing + reduced batch tokens + scale + cache trim seems to have stabilized.

jamie.oncall: customer impact summary for ops log / handoff:
- peak 5xx: 18% (11:58-12:06 UTC)
- current 5xx: 6% and trending down (12:12 UTC)
- affected segments: long-prompt enterprise customers (3 known), some self-serve free-tier users sending very long contexts
- mitigations applied: reduced batch max tokens, fallback-model routing for seq>1024, scaled pool replicas 3->8, evicted 30% KV cache, enabled gateway throttles, emergency fail-fast for >4096 seq.
- suggested follow-ups: revert fallback after 24h test, telemetry alert refinements, scheduler packing change, add canary for future max_seq rollouts.

jamie.oncall: handing off to @sarah-sre for the next 90 minutes. all actions executed; monitor for regressions and customer-reported breakages. sarah, I left the pending actions pinned in the incident checklist.

sarah-sre: taking handoff. next steps from my side: watch error rate and queue depth, coordinate with CS for active customers, prepare rollback if we see re-escalation. I'll also validate garbage collection of per-session KV metrics and check memory pressure graphs.

pagerduty-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff recorded. Incident timeline started 2026-03-14T11:58Z. Severity reduced to S2; monitoring for 2 hours.

jamie.oncall: closing thread for live mitigation; will open a postmortem doc with timeline and root-cause after we confirm stabilization. great job team :thumbsup:

sarah-sre: copying that — I'll update the incident channel if anything regresses.

ops-bot: MONITOR: service health stable for 10m. continuing to watch.
